message.content: Lions mate during a brief but intense period called the “breeding season,” which typically occurs in late winter or early spring. Male lions form coalitions—groups of related males that defend a pride together. When a coalition encounters a receptive female (usually after she has just given birth), they engage in a ritualized courtship that includes vocalizations, scent marking, and physical displays. Once the female signals readiness, the male(s) will mount her from behind, often with multiple males attempting to copulate simultaneously. Copulation lasts only a few minutes, but the male’s sperm can fertilize eggs for up to 48 hours afterward. After mating, the male may stay with the pride to guard against rival coalitions, though he does not participate in rearing the cubs.
